feedback: Written before this candidate races. Iteration 1 (±0.03 m span, 0.012 m footprint, y = 0.06 m, score 337.5) is the best result: oval 13/20 finishes at 1.83 s, but s-bend 1/20 and slalom 0/20 with max_error 0.062 to 0.063 m and 1.1 to 1.3 line-loss events per run. Iteration 2 (span ±0.04 m) dropped to 150.8 with oval finishes falling to 0/20, so widening span hurt. Iteration 3 (0.016 m footprint) dropped to 217.4 with oval finishes at 2/20 and slalom line-loss rising to 1.85, so footprint overlap did not close the gap. Note that my earlier recommendation of 0.016 m was contradicted by iteration 3, so please do not treat it as a guide. The controller is unchanged from iteration 1 in this race, so the result isolates forward position. Decision rules for the next race: if s-bend and slalom line-loss falls to about 0.5 to 1.0 per run and max_error drops below about 0.055 m with oval finishes at or above 13/20, keep y = 0.07 m and tune the weights only if oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.2. If line-loss is unchanged at about 1.1 or more with max_error near 0.06 m, forward position is not the gap, so move to turn authority. If oval finishes fall below about 10/20, return y to 0.06 m.
requested_changes: Keep the iteration 1 geometry and move only the sensor row from y = 0.06 to y = 0.07 m. Evidence: iteration 1 is the best score (337.5), and iterations 2 and 3 showed that span and footprint changes both hurt, so forward look-ahead is the untested lever.

If line-loss on s-bend and slalom stays at 1.1 or more per run with max_error near 0.06 m at y = 0.07 m, try wheel_track 0.10 m with all else unchanged. Evidence: iteration 1 turn-authority changes (wheel_track 0.12 to 0.11 with mass 0.8 to 0.7) were confounded, so this is a clean follow-up test, not a proven fix.
Do not change sensor_size or span in the next iteration. Evidence: 0.016 m footprint (iteration 3) cut oval finishes from 13/20 to 2/20, and ±0.04 m span (iteration 2) cut them to 0/20.
